getty:9148d3ac-44a4-4573-b54d-53f02f4854.summary: Inside an ornamental frame, Christ sits on a green mountaintop, raised above six disciples who stand symmetrically on either side and turn toward him. He holds a book in one hand and gestures with the other, as if answering a question, and like his apostles wears a Roman-style pallium. The painter drew the drapery in agitated spirals and zigzags that charge the balanced composition with energy.
facts: The Getty describes the leaf as coming from a Gospel book made about 1000, perhaps at Canterbury in England.
The museum notes that the artist emphasised Christ's role as teacher by placing him higher than his apostles, giving him more space and turning all of them toward him.
getty:9148d3ac-44a4-4573-b54d-53f02f4854.notes: The Getty does not tie the scene to a specific Gospel passage; the Sermon on the Mount is cited only as a theme. Much of the page around the miniature is blank and the leaf is irregularly cut.

princeton:19972.summary: The two hinged halves of this small bronze reliquary cross are shown one above the other. On the upper half a figure with outstretched arms, worn almost smooth, appears to be the crucified Christ; on the lower half the Virgin stands in a long robe with her hands raised in prayer. Worn on the breast, such crosses enclosed a relic between their two halves.
facts: Princeton records the cross as Middle Byzantine, from Ashdod in Palestine, 9th–11th century; it is only 5.8 cm high.
Pairing Christ on one leaf with the praying Virgin on the other is a common scheme of Middle Byzantine bronze reliquary crosses (type).
princeton:19972.notes: The figure of Christ is heavily worn; identification follows the museum title. The 'type' fact is general knowledge about such encolpia, not a statement about this object.
